mainTopic: Finishing שמואל's rulings on tithing the beans, how to decide which year a crop belongs to, and why the new year for trees falls in שבט
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of שמואל's three rulings: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי about the Egyptian beans, nothing counts as mixed (אין בילה), and everything follows גמר פרי. In a צריכא, the גמרא shows that each ruling is needed so we do not misread the others. It then asks why 'nothing mixes' is needed at all, and answers that it teaches that wine and oil do mix. Next, a ברייתא brings two readings of the פסוק 'when you gather from your threshing floor and winepress'. רבי יוסי הגלילי says a crop belongs to the year whose rain it actually grew on. רבי עקיבא says it depends on whether the plant lives on rain alone or also needs irrigation. רבי אבהו shows that they differ about seedless onions and Egyptian beans, and a משנה about holding back water for 30 days follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. Then the גמרא explains why the first of שבט is the new year for trees: by then most of the year's rain has fallen, even though winter is not over. The amud ends as a ברייתא begins a story about רבי עקיבא, who separated two tithes from an אתרוג picked on the first of שבט. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why we need the ruling that nothing mixes
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל had only said that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, we would think his reason is that solids mix together (יש בילה). So שמואל had to add that nothing mixes except liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to have all of שמואל's statements. If he had only taught us that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, I would have said that this is because he holds that solid items do mix together. So he teaches us: nothing mixes (except liquids).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a צריכא, explaining why שמואל needed to say all three of his statements. This first link shows why the statement 'לכל אין בילה' is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון שזורי lets the farmer put all the beans into one pile and tithe them together. A reader could easily guess that the reason is בילה, meaning the beans blend into one mass. שמואל's separate ruling that solids never mix blocks that wrong reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. This formula shows that each of several statements teaches something new.
He taught us
I would have said. This introduces the mistaken first assumption.
He comes to teach us. This introduces the correction.
Mixing. Items blend so fully that they count as one mass.
The תנא who says the beans from both years may be made into one pile

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two kinds of 'one pile' here. רבי שמעון שזורי does say you may tithe the beans together, but the reason is NOT that they mix (בילה). That is exactly the mistake this step corrects.

phrases.english: And it is necessary: for if he had taught us only
the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר יֵשׁ בִּילָּה,
phrases.english: I would have said: it is because he holds there is mixing,
phrases.notes: The wrong reason we might have assumed

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: לַכֹּל אֵין בִּילָּה.
phrases.english: so he teaches us: for everything there is no mixing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the צריכא that follows the resolution of רבי זירא's contradiction between שמואל's statements (on the previous amud).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי, standing alone, would suggest יש בילה. The statement לכל אין בילה is needed to block that reading.

steps.title: Why we need the ruling that follows רבי שמעון שזורי
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל had only said that nothing mixes, we would think he agrees with the רבנן, who forbid tithing the two years' beans together. So he had to say that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught us that nothing mixes, I would have said that he holds like the רבנן, so the beans could not be tithed together. So he teaches us that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second link of the צריכא. It flips the first link and shows why the ruling for רבי שמעון שזורי is also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you only knew 'אין בילה', the natural conclusion would be that each batch stays separate. That would mean the farmer cannot tithe from one batch for the other, which is the view of the רבנן. The explicit ruling for רבי שמעון שזורי shows that he still allows one pile, for a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue with רבי שמעון שזורי. They hold the two batches belong to separate tithe years.
He holds (this opinion)
Tithe. Produce of one year cannot be tithed for produce of another year.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only that for everything there is no mixing —
I would have said: he holds like the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי.
phrases.english: so he teaches us: the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 1. It shows that the second statement alone would also be misread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The statement אין בילה, standing alone, would suggest the ruling follows the רבנן. The ruling for רבי שמעון שזורי is needed to block that.

steps.title: Why we need the rule that everything follows full ripening
steps.stepSummary: Even with both statements, we would think שמואל contradicts himself, as רבי זירא asked. So שמואל had to give his third statement: everything follows גמר פרי. That is the real reason רבי שמעון שזורי allows one pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught us these two statements, I would have said that שמואל contradicts שמואל. So he teaches us that everything follows the full ripening of the fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third link of the צריכא. It shows that the third statement, הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי, is what makes the first two fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only the first two statements, there would be a contradiction: why allow one pile if nothing mixes? The third statement gives the true reason. All the beans finish ripening at the same time, so they belong to one tithe year, and no mixing is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: These two (statements)
A difficulty or contradiction
The full ripening of the produce. Here it sets which tithe year the produce belongs to.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the hidden logic of the whole סוגיא. רבי שמעון שזורי's ruling rests on when the produce ripens, not on mixing.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only these two —
I would have said: Shmuel's statement contradicts Shmuel's other statement,
phrases.notes: This refers back to רבי זירא's question

phrases.english: so he teaches us:
everything follows the full ripening of the fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on steps 1 and 2 by showing that their combination still needs the third statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third statement, הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי, is needed to settle the apparent contradiction between the first two.

steps.title: The full-ripening rule is limited to the disputed cases
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל had only said that everything follows גמר פרי, we would apply it even to grain and olives. So he also said that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in the case he argued about. That limits the rule to cases like the beans.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught us that everything follows the full ripening of the fruit, I would have said that this applies even to grain and olives. So he teaches us that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי in the case where he disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final link of the צריכא. It shows that the ruling for רבי שמעון שזורי is still needed to mark the limits of the גמר פרי rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הכל' (everything) could make us think the ripening rule covers all produce. But grain and olives follow a different marker: reaching one-third of their growth (הבאת שליש). Tying the ripening rule to 'במאי דפליג' keeps it only in the bean case that רבי שמעון שזורי argued about.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain
Olives
In the case that he argues about
One-third growth. This is the marker that sets the tithe year for grain and olives.

steps.whatToRemember: Each of שמואל's three statements is needed. (1) Without 'אין בילה', we would think רבי שמעון שזורי's reason is mixing. (2) Without the ruling for רבי שמעון שזורי, we would follow the רבנן. (3) Without 'גמר פרי', שמואל would seem to contradict himself. (4) Without limiting the rule to 'במאי דפליג', we would wrongly apply גמר פרי to grain and olives.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only
that everything follows the full ripening of the fruit —
I would have said:
even grain and olives as well —
phrases.notes: In fact, these follow the stage of one-third growth

phrases.english: so he teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי בְּמַאי דִּפְלִיג.
phrases.english: the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon Shezuri in the case where he disagrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר גְּמַר פֶּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא by showing that the third statement, standing alone, would also be stretched too far.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three statements of שמואל are needed. The rule of גמר פרי applies only where רבי שמעון שזורי disagrees, as with the beans, and not to grain and olives, which follow שליש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The statement הכל הולך אחר גמר פרי, standing alone, would be applied even to grain and olives. The ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי במאי דפליג is needed to limit it to the disputed case.

steps.title: Why did שמואל need the statement 'nothing mixes'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי and that everything follows גמר פרי, why did he also need to say that nothing mixes?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him teach us only these two statements. Why do I need 'nothing mixes'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for one of שמואל's three statements. It says two statements seem to be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 showed that the גמר פרי rule is the real reason behind רבי שמעון שזורי. Step 4 showed that 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי' limits that rule to beans. So the גמרא now asks what the statement 'nothing mixes' still adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him teach us
These two (statements)
Mixing: when items mix together and are treated as one batch
Why do I need it? (asks why something is said at all)

phrases.english: But let him teach us these two (statements) alone;
phrases.notes: These are 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי' and 'everything follows גמר פרי'.

phrases.english: why do I need 'nothing mixes'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַשְׁמְעִינַן הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי, לַכֹּל אֵין בִּילָּה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 3 and 4 explained why the other two statements are needed, the גמרא now asks about the remaining one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two statements already give the full ruling and its limits, the third one seems extra.

steps.title: It teaches that wine and oil do mix
steps.stepSummary: The statement 'nothing mixes' is needed to teach that liquids like wine and oil do mix.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: wine and oil do mix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The real point of 'nothing mixes except liquids' is the exception: liquids do mix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new information is not about solids, since that is already clear. It is about liquids. Wine and oil from two years that are mixed together are treated as truly mixed.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it comes to teach us
Wine and oil (liquids)

steps.whatToRemember: Each of שמואל's three statements has its own job. 'The הלכה follows רבי שמעון שזורי' limits the case to beans. 'Everything follows גמר פרי' gives the reason. 'Nothing mixes except liquids' teaches that wine and oil do mix.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that for wine and oil there is mixing.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the statement is needed for its exception (liquids), not for its main rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is needed to teach that wine and oil do mix.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: it depends on which year's water the plant grows on
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the פסוק that anything that grows on last year's water is tithed with last year. Vegetables grow on next year's water, so they are tithed with next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: 'When you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.' Grain and grapes grow on last year's water and are tithed with last year. So anything that grows on last year's water is tithed with last year. This leaves out vegetables, which grow on next year's water and are tithed with next year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ברייתא. רבי יוסי הגלילי gives a rule for which year a crop belongs to for מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions grain (threshing floor) and grapes (winepress). They grow mostly from the rain of the past winter, and they belong to the past year. רבי יוסי הגלילי makes this the rule: whatever grows on last year's water goes with last year. Vegetables grow fast on the new rains, so they go with the new year.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא
Threshing floor and winepress (stand for grain and grapes)
They are tithed
The water (rain) of last year
Vegetables

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
"When you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress" (Devarim 16:13);
just as the threshing floor and winepress are special
in that they grow on the water of last year,
and are tithed for last year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁגְּדֵילִין עַל מֵי שָׁנָה שֶׁעָבְרָה —
phrases.english: so too, anything that grows on the water of last year
is tithed for last year.

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאוּ יְרָקוֹת שֶׁגְּדֵילִין עַל מֵי שָׁנָה הַבָּאָה,
phrases.english: This excludes vegetables, which grow on the water of the coming year,
and are tithed for the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about how to decide which year produce belongs to for מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce that grows on last year's water is tithed with last year. Vegetables, which grow on next year's water, are tithed with next year.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: it depends on 'most water' versus 'all water'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from the same פסוק that anything that grows on 'most water' (rain is enough) is tithed with last year. Vegetables need 'all water' (also irrigation), so they are tithed with next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'When you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.' Grain and grapes grow on most water and are tithed with last year. So anything that grows on most water is tithed with last year. This leaves out vegetables, which grow on all water and are tithed with next year.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי עקיבא, who learns from the same פסוק but gives a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not ask which year's rain the plant used. He asks what kind of plant it is. If it lives on rain alone ('most water'), it goes with last year. If it also needs watering by hand ('all water'), like vegetables, it goes with the new year.

keyTerms.meaning: Most water: rain alone is enough for the plant
All water: the plant needs irrigation too

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים reach the same result for grain and for normal vegetables. They only differ in how they define the rule. That is exactly why the גמרא will ask next, 'what is the difference between them?'

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"When you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress";
just as the threshing floor and winepress are special
in that they grow on most water,
and are tithed for last year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁגְּדֵילִין עַל רוֹב מַיִם —
phrases.english: so too, anything that grows on most water
is tithed for last year.

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאוּ יְרָקוֹת שֶׁגְּדֵילִין עַל כׇּל מַיִם,
phrases.english: This excludes vegetables, which grow on all water,
and are tithed for the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same פסוק, with a different rule from רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce that grows on rain alone is tithed with last year. Produce that needs irrigation (vegetables) is tithed with next year.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the views of רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא would actually lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks for a case where the two views give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree about grain, grapes, and normal vegetables. So the גמרא wants a case where the two definitions really split apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the two views just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא would rule differently.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: seedless onions and Egyptian beans
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the difference shows up with seedless onions and Egyptian beans.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The difference between them is seedless onions and Egyptian beans.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו names the case where the two views split. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These plants are normally watered like vegetables, so their type is 'all water'. But a farmer can stop watering them before ראש השנה, and then they actually grow on last year's water. רבי יוסי הגלילי looks at the actual water, so the farmer's choice matters. רבי עקיבא looks at the type of plant, so it would not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Seedless onions (grown for their greens)
Egyptian bean (cowpea)
There is a difference between them

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Seedless onions and the Egyptian bean
are the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: בְּצָלִים הַסָּרִיסִין וּפוֹל הַמִּצְרִי אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Seedless onions and Egyptian beans, which a farmer can stop watering before ראש השנה.

steps.title: The משנה: it depends on whether water was held back for 30 days
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that if the farmer held back water from these plants for 30 days before ראש השנה, they go with last year. If not, they go with the new year. This fits רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Seedless onions and Egyptian beans that the farmer held back water from for thirty days before ראש השנה are tithed for last year, and they are permitted in שביעית. If not, they are forbidden in שביעית and are tithed for the coming year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו brings a משנה to show that this case is the real difference. The משנה decides the year based on the actual watering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה judges the same plant differently based on what the farmer did. That matches רבי יוסי הגלילי, who goes by which year's water the plant actually grew on. According to רבי עקיבא, the type of plant ('all water') decides, so holding back water would not change the year.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
He held back water from them
The seventh year (שמיטה)
And if not

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the year depends on which year's water the plant actually grew on. רבי עקיבא: it depends on the type of plant (rain only, or needs irrigation). The משנה about seedless onions and Egyptian beans follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that for מעשר and שביעית, a farmer's actions (like stopping watering) can change which year a crop belongs to, at least according to the view the משנה follows.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Seedless onions and the Egyptian bean
from which one held back water
thirty days before Rosh HaShana
are tithed for the past year
and are permitted in the Seventh Year;
and if not,
they are forbidden in the Seventh Year
and are tithed for the coming year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רבי אבהו's answer in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That seedless onions and Egyptian beans are where רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא differ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (שביעית 2:9) that makes the year depend on holding back water for 30 days before ראש השנה.

steps.title: Why is the first of שבט the new year for trees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the first of שבט is the ראש השנה for trees. It asks what the reason is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'On the first of שבט is the new year for trees.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה about trees and asks why that date was picked. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about vegetables and which year they are tithed with. Now the גמרא moves to trees. The משנה gives a date with no reason, so the גמרא asks for the logic behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: The new year for trees. It decides which year's tithes a tree's fruit belongs to.
The Hebrew month that comes in the middle of winter.
What is the reason?

phrases.english: On the first of Shevat is the new year for trees.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The משנה says this is the view of בית שמאי. בית הלל say the fifteenth of שבט.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of vegetables to a new line in the משנה about trees.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the new year for trees is set on the first of שבט.

steps.title: Most of the year's rain has already fallen
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי אושעיא, says the reason is that by the first of שבט most of the year's rain has fallen, while most of the winter season is still to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: because most of the year's rain has already fallen, and most of the season is still outside, meaning still to come.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the question. He says the date was picked because most of the rain for the year has already come down by then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tree fruit that starts to grow after most of the rain has fallen is treated as growing on the new year's rain, so it counts as new-year fruit. The second half of the answer, that most of winter is still ahead, is confusing. Why would that support the date? The next step asks exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because.
The rains of the year.
A season. Here it means the winter season, which lasts until about ניסן.
Outside. Here it means still remaining, not yet finished.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
Since most of the year's rains have gone out (already fallen),
and most of the season is still outside (still to come).
phrases.notes: This line is unclear, and the גמרא asks about it next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By the first of שבט most of the year's rain has fallen, so new growth belongs to the next year.

steps.title: What does this answer mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אושעיא meant, since the second half of his answer seems to work against his own reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask how to read רבי אושעיא's words. This sets up an explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement is phrased as two reasons joined by 'and'. But 'most of winter is still ahead' does not sound like a reason to start the new year. If anything, it sounds like a reason to wait. The גמרא is not attacking him. It wants to know how his words fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? Used to ask for the meaning of an unclear statement.

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the wording of the answer in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the clause 'most of the season is still outside' fits into the reason.

steps.title: Even though winter isn't over, most of the rain is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the clause about winter means 'even though'. Even though most of winter is still ahead, most of the rain has already fallen, and that is what decides the matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: even though most of the season is still to come, since most of the year's rains have already fallen, the new year for trees begins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads רבי אושעיא's words. The point about winter is not a second reason. It answers an objection someone might raise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the tree year should not start while winter is still going on. The answer is that this does not matter. The amount of rain is what counts, and by the first of שבט most of it has fallen. So fruit that grows from then on belongs to the next year.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. It introduces an explanation of someone's words.
Even though.

steps.whatToRemember: The ראש השנה for trees follows the rain, not the calendar season. Once most of the year's rain has fallen, which happens by שבט, the tree year turns over, even though winter is not finished.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרוֹב תְּקוּפָה מִבַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: Even though most of the season is still to come,
since most of the year's rains have already fallen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by rereading 'and still' as 'even though'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The winter clause means 'even though', not a second reason. Rain is the deciding factor.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא picks an אתרוג on the first of שבט
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins a story: רבי עקיבא picked an אתרוג on the first of שבט and separated two tithes from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: there was an incident with רבי עקיבא, who picked an אתרוג on the first of שבט and treated it with two tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a story about רבי עקיבא, connected to the date it just discussed. The story continues past this point, so this step sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some years of the seven-year cycle require מעשר שני and others require מעשר עני. רבי עקיבא picked the fruit right on the borderline date and was unsure which year it belonged to. So he separated both tithes.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. It introduces a ברייתא.
An incident; a story about what really happened.
A citron fruit. Its tree is famous for keeping fruit growing on it for a long time.
Two tithes. Here this means both מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי and מַעֲשַׂר עָנִי.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Two tithes' does not mean he gave double out of extra piety. He was in doubt whether the fruit belonged to a year that requires מעשר שני or a year that requires מעשר עני, so he separated both to cover either case.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An incident with Rabbi Akiva
who picked an etrog on the first of Shevat
and treated it with two tithes,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story tied to the date of the first of שבט just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא separated both מעשר שני and מעשר עני from an אתרוג picked on the first of שבט, because he was in doubt which year it belonged to.
